Why this course
9 in 10
developers use Git.
Stack Overflow Developer Survey, 2022. GitHub is where most of that work is shared.
Your GitHub profile becomes your portfolio.
Recruiters and teammates look at it. What you build in this course can live there.
Two different things

Git is the engine. GitHub is the garage.

Git
Software on your laptop that records every change. Works offline. Next class.
GitHub
A website that stores your projects online, so you can back them up and share them. Today.

The key word

A repository is a project folder with a memory.

It holds your files, plus the full history of every change: who changed what, and when.
People shorten it to repo. One project, one repo.

Who can see it?

Public or private.

Public
Anyone on the internet can see it. Only you, and people you add, can change it. Good for portfolio work.
Private
Only you, and people you invite, can see it. Good for unfinished work or anything personal.
Never put passwords or API keys in any repo, public or private.

Cheat sheet

Six Markdown symbols.

You typeYou get
# TitleA big heading (## for smaller)
**bold**bold text
*italic*italic text
- itemA bullet list
[text](https://link)A clickable link
`code`code in a box
Edit on the website

Pencil, edit, Commit changes.

1
Open README.md, click the pencil icon
2
Edit, then check the Preview tab
3
Click Commit changes
Type a short message saying what you changed.
Remember this word
commit
A saved version with a message. GitHub runs Git for you when you press that button. Next class, you run Git yourself.
Removing data

Delete one file.

1
Click the file to open it
2
Open the ⋯ menu at the top right of the file
3
Choose Delete file
4
Commit changes
Yes, deleting is a commit too.
The old version is still in history.
Deleting removes it from the latest version, not from past commits. That is why secrets must never be committed.
The nuclear option

Delete a whole repository.

1
Open the repo, click Settings
2
Scroll to the Danger Zone
3
Delete this repository
GitHub asks you to confirm, by typing the repo name.

Recap

Four questions.

01
What is a repository?
A project folder plus the full history of its changes.
02
What is README.md for?
The front page of the repo, written in Markdown.
03
Where do you change visibility?
Settings, Danger Zone, Change visibility.
04
What does Commit changes do?
Saves a new version with a message. That is a commit.
